articles.title: Pit Lane Ghost
articles.summary: Diagonal fine hatch of lane ticks and corner tabs, worn scuffs; light, sketchy, low-contrast sheen. Reads as a busy scratched or hatched texture; on satin the dashed diagonal lines stay visible as rail-like stripes in the highlight.
articles.what: Fine pit-stall corners and service-box outlines combine with independently placed lane ticks, corner tabs, worn scuffs and witness dots. Up close: A dense scribble of tiny angular marks about 15 px, ticks, corners and L-shapes, tilted and tiled like scratchy hatching. On satin the highlight also lights up long dashed diagonal lines, like lane markings; on metallic those lines vanish and the scribble shows as dull grey marks on the bright band. From a distance: Reads as a busy scratched or hatched texture; on satin the dashed diagonal lines stay visible as rail-like stripes in the highlight. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Track & Motorsport (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, sides, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Track & Motorsport", or search for "Pit Lane Ghost".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: wide panels show the hatch
Rockers and lower panels for a worn feel
Busy hatch; bold numbers read, thin numbers get noisy.
Best use: bright dashed lane lines through the highlight over a scratchy hatch
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not brushed metal: broken angular marks, not long straight streaks (except the dashed lines on satin)
Not real scratches colour: shine only, no paint damage
Avoid: diagonal clashes with stripes, faint on light bases.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Pit Lane Ghost over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
